final_answer: Ice floats on water because of its molecular structure. When water freezes, the molecules arrange themselves into a hexagonal lattice, creating open spaces between them. This arrangement makes ice less dense than liquid water. Because of its lower density, ice displaces more water than its own weight, allowing it to float. This unique behavior is due to hydrogen bonding between water molecules, which stabilizes the hexagonal structure in ice. This property is essential for the survival of aquatic life in cold climates.
